text: {"status":"NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT","core_findings":["Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show weaker sampled training separation: negatives beat positives at 11.49% and 12.42% of supervised positions, versus 3.38% for Movies_and_TV and 4.68% for CDs_and_Vinyl.","Appended-MASK user representations are more concentrated in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics (RankMe 11.71 and 16.09) than in Movies_and_TV and CDs_and_Vinyl (32.52 and 24.58); item RankMe remains 47.88–51.59, so these measurements do not establish wholesale representation collapse."],"key_implications":["Sampled training discrimination is stronger for Movies_and_TV and CDs_and_Vinyl; these probes do not establish validation HR@10.","User representation concentration accompanies weaker separation in the two harder categories, but the measurements do not establish causality.","Training branch allocation is unavailable; diagnostic terminal-position coverage cannot establish the training objective's branch balance."],"evidence":{"headline_metrics":{"Industrial_and_Scientific:pos_neg_margin_p10":-0.1487,"Electronics:pos_neg_margin_p10":-0.2356,"Industrial_and_Scientific:appended_mask_users_rankme":11.714,"Electronics:appended_mask_users_rankme":16.094},"brief_metric_read":{"pos_neg_margin_p10":"Negative lower-tail margins indicate incorrectly ordered positive–negative pairs.","appended_mask_users_rankme":"Lower effective rank indicates a more concentrated centered user spectrum, not conclusive collapse."}}}
